content:
You can already set ChatGPT as your default digital assistant on Android, but so far it's been limited to voice conversations and text replies. Today, strings found in version 1.2026.328 of the Android app suggest OpenAI is working on giving it much deeper control over your phone.
The leftover permission prompts mention letting ChatGPT look up your contacts, read recent calls, place phone calls when you ask, and read and send text messages. All of this would require you to grant the relevant permissions first.
The app also appears to be preparing a way to find and control media playing on your phone. It would use Android's notification access to pause, resume, or skip tracks. That said, it reportedly wouldn't be able to open a music app or start a new song on its own. It would only resume an existing session.
ChatGPT may also be able to look at what's currently visible on your screen and use that as context for your questions. The strings point to a "Use screen and app data" toggle, and they suggest the assistant would take a fresh look at the display for every follow-up about it.
Some of the other permissions mention a "Dot card", which likely refers to ChatGPT's Dots, the agents that can carry out tasks without you keeping the app open. Two configuration flags in the code, "allowedWhileLocked" and "useDotAsAssistant", hint that a Dot could be used even when the phone is locked, or even set as the device's digital assistant. There's no word on when any of this might actually show up, or whether all of it will, so we'll let you know if and when it does.
